claims.statement: simulator::agent_protocol publicly exposes only its own headers and nlohmann_json; its Windows system libraries (bcrypt, advapi32, user32, ws2_32) are private, and it links no simulator or UI target.

simulator::agent_api links the protocol library, UI-free editor services, the network-analyzer, spectrum-analyzer, and power-meter engines, the test-flow and Touchstone libraries, and Threads, and it does not link simulator::app or any UI library.
simulator::mcp_adapter exposes only the protocol library and Threads publicly and keeps logging private; rf-sim-mcp links the adapter privately and installs into bin.
rf-sim-mcp answers MCP discovery and tools/list without a reachable GUI and accepts --endpoint, --version, and --help.
The API reaches application behavior only through IAgentHost, a seven-method interface, and circuit edits still route through EditorCommands.
AppAgentHost implements IAgentHost, and RfSimulatorApp owns the AgentApi, the AgentServer, and the server opt-in as members.

AppAgentHost owns checkpoints (newest 20), the activity ring, node placement, modal detection, and the project-name query, while AgentPanelWidget only renders status, the bridge path, activity, checkpoints, and a confirmation-only revert.
The Agent Server is off by default; src/main.cpp calls startAgentServerIfEnabled() after constructing the app, and enabling or disabling the server writes the persisted [Agent] ServerEnabled key.
RfSimulatorApp::update_dsp() calls AgentServer::pump() at the start of every frame, before the circuit runtime updates.

The GUI listener thread handles framing and validated envelopes only and shares just a mutex-protected inbox, outbox, connection status, and pump-refreshed epoch snapshot with the UI thread; pump() on the UI thread checks modal state and invokes the executor in FIFO order.
The bridge reads stdin on a reader thread, runs McpSession on a session thread, and dispatches queued calls serially in arrival order on one caller thread.
The GUI listener binds only the IPv4 loopback address on an ephemeral port, and AgentListener::accept closes any accepted peer that is not on loopback.
The server accepts one client: while a client is connected, a second connection receives a BUSY reply with the message another agent is connected, and is closed.
The bridge hello must present the bridge token, checked with agentTokensEqual, and the GUI token is a separately generated token that is regenerated until it differs from the bridge token.

generateAgentToken() draws 32 bytes from the OS CSPRNG (BCryptGenRandom on Windows, getrandom on Linux) and returns 64 lowercase hex characters; without a usable source it returns no token rather than weaker entropy.
agentTokensEqual returns false for unequal lengths and otherwise ORs per-byte XOR differences across the whole value before deciding.
The endpoint file is agent-endpoint-<install>.json in the directory from defaultAgentEndpointDirectory(), where <install> is the 16-hex FNV-1a of the weakly canonical executable directory.

On POSIX the endpoint directory must be owned by the current user with mode 0700 and no group or other bits; endpoint temp files are created 0600 with O_EXCL and O_NOFOLLOW; writes and token-gated removals hold an exclusive flock on the directory. On Windows, current-user-only DACLs are applied from SDDL strings.

The listener and each accepted channel are close-on-exec: Linux uses SOCK_CLOEXEC and accept4, other POSIX systems set FD_CLOEXEC after creation or accept, and Windows sockets are not inherited because the runner's CreateProcessW passes bInheritHandles FALSE.
Inbound lines are capped at 1 MiB (kAgentMaxLineBytes), and JSON nested deeper than 64 containers (kAgentMaxJsonDepth) is refused by an iterative check before any recursive copy or dump.

The catalog defines exactly ten v1 tools (component_types, library_search, circuit_get, component_get, circuit_edit, measure_port, network_analyzer_sweep, data_file_read, test_flow_run, receiver_measure), and kAgentCatalogVersion is 1.
Within one catalog version, changes are additive; removing or retyping a field or tool requires a version increment.

No catalog tool grants extension trust, runs external tools, authors component-library entries, imports or exports .rflib files, or opens, saves, or names a file; data_file_read takes no paths and never writes, and agents may read only data files a component or library part already references.
The bridge verifies the GUI token and catalog version before relaying a call; a malformed reply or JSON-RPC error drops the channel, and a later call reconnects.

The MCP session selects a protocol era per request: legacy initialization-era versions 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25, or the stateless 2026-07-28 era, which carries its own version and capability metadata.
